newsitem.title: UK: European low and high sulphur fuel spread widens.
newsitem.headline: European low and high sulphur fuel spread widens.

text.p: The spread between high and low sulphur European fuel oil widened on Tuesday as cargo swaps firmed while barge prices fell away, traders said.

After a morning of healthy trade boosted by post-holiday bunker demand prices for high sulphur barges slipped back. Most deals were then done at $84 and $83 fob a tonne, $1 lower than Monday's notional prices.
"Numbers went down for no specific apparent reason other than that one guy was wanting to have a bigger share of the market," said one Rotterdam-based trader.
Low sulphur swaps were pushed up by stronger crude, with June done at $98 late in the day. However, no physical deals were seen to match that number.
"No one has come forward with any firm availabilities after Friday's deal (at $95 fob) which rather shook the market," said one producer. "People are keeping rather quiet."

The U.S.-based trader who bought British low sulphur barrels at the end of last week was heard to have bought 25,000 tonnes of bunker spec high sulphur material on the same day on a floating price basis.
Traders speculated the material would be co-loaded for trans-Atlantic shipment.
But high sulphur markets were said to be over-supplied, with cracked Russian fuel oil from the summer inland export programme weighing on markets.
The material was heard bid in Rotterdam at below barge prices and was being offered to European utilities.
